author: Australian Associated Press
description:
NSW supreme court judge otherwise dismisses case brought by film’s co-producers and awards Wilson almost $400,000 after star countersued

Australian A-lister Rebel Wilson has secured a major court victory after co-producers of her debut film accused her of sabotage, lying and breaching contracts.

The Pitch Perfect star directed, co-produced and starred in The Deb, a musical comedy that became the battleground for multiple legal battles in Australia and the US.

Continue reading...
title: Rebel Wilson secures another Australian court win as co-producers of The Deb awarded just $10

author: Giles Richards in Austin
description:
• 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’

  • Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record

Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s, with the seven-time world champion also stating he believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.

Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the
title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
City’s council passed Romanch’s Law, named after teen who died when he was ejected from carriage earlier this year

The New York city council has voted to ban horse-drawn carriage rides in the city by 2028 in a decision that has widespread implications for hundreds of jobs.

The council voted on Thursday on Romanch’s Law, legislation named in memory of 18-year-old Romanch Mahajan, who died this summer after he was ejected from a runaway horse-drawn carriage in Central Park.

Continue reading...
title: New York city council votes to ban horse-drawn carriage rides

author: Maya Yang
description:
Musk’s investment into the new media empire comes after Paramount’s $111bn merger with Warner Bros Discovery

Elon Musk has reportedly invested approximately $1bn in Skydance, the new media empire led by David Ellison.

The deal comes alongside fresh equity infusions from existing investors, including board member Laurene Powell Jobs, Steve Jobs’s widow. Semafor first reported the news.

Continue reading...
title: Elon Musk reportedly invests $1bn in David Ellison’s Skydance

author: Adrian Horton
description:
Actors in the mix to play 007 in Denis Villeneuve’s installment include Callum Turner and Jack Lowden

The search for the next James Bond may finally be nearing its end: according to reports, a very select group of actors will screen-test to become the next British agent 007 this weekend.

According to the Hollywood Reporter and Variety, citing several sources, a group of actors reportedly including Callum Turner and Slow Horses’ Jack Lowden, will appear in front of cameras as the secret agent this weekend in London.

Continue reading...
title: James Bond finalists to screen-test for role this week – reports

author: Benjamin Lee
description:
Actor also had roles in M*A*S*H, A River Runs Through It and Picket Fences in career spanning 60 years

Tom Skerritt, the actor known for roles in Alien and Top Gun, has died at the age of 93.

His publicist confirmed to Variety that he died from natural causes.

Continue reading...
title: Tom Skerritt, Alien and Top Gun actor, dies aged 93

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Becky Drury says she was hit by gunfire before she could intervene in attack that killed four, including three children

A teacher wounded in last week’s shooting at a Bend, Oregon, elementary school shared her account of the incident, and how she was shot before she could intervene and “[pretended] to be dead”.

Becky Drury was seriously wounded at Silver Rail elementary when Griffin J John II, a 16-year-old former student at the school armed with a shotgun, broke in and headed toward a special education classroom. He shot six people, killing Megan Lambert, a 25-year-old teacher, and three children, including five-year-old Rhoam Summer.

Continue reading...
title: Teacher wounded in Oregon school shooting played dead after she was shot

author: Alice Speri
description:
‘Political candidates’ once reflexive support for Israel has increasingly become a liability

When the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, the most prominent pro-Israel lobby group in the US, announced on Wednesday that it would stop endorsing candidates or make direct contributions to them, its many critics were quick to hail the development as Aipac’s admission of how toxic its brand had become.

The announcement marked a significant reversal that underscored just how profoundly US public opinion of Israel has shifted over the latest war in Gaza, and how political candidates’ once reflexive support for Israel has increa
title: Aipac halts candidate endorsements amid US backlash against Israel

author: Owen Myers
description:
A stage show based on the late singer is reportedly set to feature her best-loved songs with involvement from her father Mitch

A musical based on Amy Winehouse is in development for London’s West End.

The project is still in early stages with Catherine Schreiber, a Tony award-winning producer(Cabaret, Rent), attached to the project, according to Variety. Casting is reported to currently be underway.

Continue reading...
title: Amy Winehouse musical in development for West End

description:
Lawmakers in Albania's parliament clashed on Thursday as opposition MPs attempted to disrupt a session, throwing objects and ripping microphones from the desks of members of the ruling majority. Several opposition MPs held up images of students injured by police during protests in the capital, Tirana

Continue reading...
title: Scuffle breaks out in Albanian parliament over student protests – video

author: Taha Hashim
description:
• Liyanage hits six for win with one ball to spare

  • England captain’s record innings not enough

Harry Brook pulverised his way to the fastest double hundred in ODI history and it still was not enough for England. Sri Lanka were the victors in this absurd contest, hauling down a target of 430 in Rawalpindi, the second-highest successful chase in the history of the format. Only that magical 438 game, 20 years ago, trumps it.

Pavan Rathnayake, Dasun Shanaka and Avishka Fernando were the headliners, somehow turning it around for Sri Lanka after they were reduced to 24 for two. Rathnayake top-scored with 130, Fernando struck 97, and Shanaka – with 97 of his own – was the most brutal of the lot.

Continue reading...
title: Sri Lanka stun England with second-highest ODI chase despite Brook’s 202

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Lendeborg takes issue with appeals for foul calls

  • Forward says he had limited exposure to league

Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had an extraordinary NBA debut as he jawed with Luka Dončić and admitted he had largely been exposed to the league through highlights before turning professional.

Lendeborg was given the task of guarding the Los Angeles Lakers star for large parts of Wednesday’s game, which Dončić’s team won 127-105.

Continue reading...
title: Rookie Lendeborg jaws at ‘weak ass’ Dončić and admits he didn’t watch much NBA

author: Associated Press
description:
The social media personality denies allegations he gave a girl alcohol until she was drunk and sexually assaulted her

The “looksmaxxing” livestreamer Braden Peters, better known by his stage name Clavicular, pleaded not guilty Thursday to charges that he raped a 17-year-old girl at his family’s Massachusetts home.

A social media personality known for promoting extreme devotion to male beauty, Peters, 20, is accused of giving the girl alcohol until she was drunk and then sexually assaulting her when she visited him in Chatham, on Cape Cod, in May 2025.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Looksmaxxing’ influencer Clavicular pleads not guilty to raping teen

author: Catherine Shoard
description:
Exclusive: Michael Aboud, whose actions in what he believed to be a documentary are likely to come under considerable scrutiny, has expressed anger at the film-maker

• This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?

The chair of the El Paso County Republican Party has said he intends to sue Sacha Baron Cohen over footage of the local politician used in new satircal comedy Ali G: Who Iz I?

In the film, Michael Aboud is shown taking part in a training programme with another Cohen character, ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad, who instructs Aboud and fellow Maga sympathisers in self-defence techniques including the wearing, over clothes, of protective plastic buttocks. He also schools them in how to fire bullets from the middle of these buttocks by the repeated up and down manipulation of a rubber penis.
title: Republican leader embarrassed by Ali G film says he plans to sue Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘A liar and a pervert’

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Hegseth’s aides, who attempted to move 30in fragile globe themselves, dropped it during relocation, army officials say

A priceless pre-second world war globe coveted by the US defence secretary Pete Hegseth for his office in the Pentagon was damaged by his staff in a botched attempt to relocate it, army officials have admitted.

Photographs published by the Washington Post on Thursday show the shattered 30-inch Eisenhower globe, said to have been used by Dwight D Eisenhower, the 34th US president, as he plotted the D-day landings as allied supreme commander.

Continue reading...
title: Pete Hegseth’s staff break priceless historic globe he requested for office

author: Lucy Small
description:
A culture of silence has buried the stories of women who allege sexual assault in surf industry settings

When news broke last week that a surfer had been provisionally suspended from international competition, after what the International Surfing Association (ISA) described as “recent reports of serious allegations of abuse within the surfing community,” the response online was unprecedented in the world of surfing.

While investigations into those allegations are ongoing, the story prompted a deluge of comments detailing other alleged experiences of sexual misconduct and assault in surf industry settings, ranging from corporate brand houses in Hawaii to organised surf trips. While horrifying, for women who have existed in this subculture across the decades, those broader stories are sadly no surprise.

Lucy Small is a professional surfer, journalist and film-maker from Sydney, with a special interest in women’s sport
title: Surfing faces a cultural reckoning as women’s voices grow louder over sexual abuse allegations | Lucy Small

author: Natasha May
description:
When stomach bugs meet turbulence, air travel can become a health hazard for all onboard – and it happens, unfortunately, ‘more regularly than you would think’

A little over an hour into their transatlantic flight, Kate Carson’s daughters had just lain down to sleep when suddenly their Air New Zealand “cuddle class” skycouch became a “nightmare” scene.

A stomach bug that had been troubling their family during the holiday reared its head again: her youngest, three years old, started throwing up. “The first time, she was asleep, and no one saw it coming, and it went all into the seat … down the side and into the crack,” Carson says.

Continue reading...
title: Delays, deodorant and ripped up carpet: how airlines handle mid-flight ‘biological hazards’

author: Rebecca Shaw
description:
I was reducing a creative life down to public recognition. Anne Carson’s career deserves more respect than that, and so does mine

I am one of those funny little people who is creative and has made the dubious decision to try to make a career out of it.

I didn’t fully commit until I was around 30, and I’ve spent the last 14 years in an up and down ride, trying to chip away until I reach the mysterious and elusive level of success where nothing bad happens ever.

Continue reading...
title: I longed for my big break. Then a Nobel winner and my girlfriend showed me why success isn’t everything | Rebecca Shaw

author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
description:
Age-related macular degeneration has also left actor, 91, unable to read or recognise faces any more

Judi Dench has said she can no longer perform on stage or in films because of her deteriorating eyesight, more than a decade after revealing she had been diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration.

“I can’t be on stage. I can’t do a play any more. I can’t do a film any more. I can’t read any more,” the 91-year-old actor told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Judi Dench says sight loss means she can no longer perform but she is still ‘besotted by’ Shakespeare’s sonnets

author: Guardian community team
description:
We’d like to hear from people living close to the Strait of Hormuz about how everyday life and the local environment have been affected by the conflict

Iranian attacks on container ships in the Strait of Hormuz have increased in recent weeks. Iran reported that seven tankers were struck on Wednesday night and over the last fortnight at least 15 container ships, passing through the waterway, were hit.

Most of the recent attacks have occurred close to the coast with Oman, a route that Iran sees as unauthorised. In the seven days to Friday 16 October, 12 vessels were attacked, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO). There are concerns that spillage fro
title: Tell us: do you live near the Strait of Hormuz? How is the US-Iran conflict affecting your life?

author: Clive Paget
description:
London Philharmonic Orchestra/Gardner
(LPO)
Edward Gardner and the LPO are taut and dramatically alert in fine performances of these two theatrical works

Recordings of The Miraculous Mandarin used to outnumber The Wooden Prince 10 to one, so it’s good to see Bartók’s earlier ballet getting equal billing here. Unlike the Mandarin with its grimy, urban, modernist vibe, the Prince is rooted in pungent Hungarian folk music, viewed, of course, through the composer’s unique 20th-century lens.

It’s the story of a princess who falls in love with a decoy prince rather than the real thing and Edward Gardner revels in the vivid colours of its nature-inflected score. The London Philharmonic Orchestra is taut and dramatically alert throughout. There’s an unnerving sense of foreboding underpinning the Dance of the Trees; the Dance of the Waves churns with kinetic energy and the foot-stamping Dance of the Princess with the Wooden Doll cuts a rus
title: Bartók: Miraculous Mandarin Suite, The Wooden Prince album review – vivid colours and astute pacing

author: Nicola Davis Science Correspondent
description:
With the climate crisis and diseases threatening one of the world’s most popular fruits, researchers are hoping a breakthrough in breeding techniques could give the Cavendish banana a certain future

Love them or loathe them, bananas are one of the world’s most popular fruit. But a combination of the climate crisis and new killer diseases have had growers concerned over the banana’s threatened extinction, something that would impose a huge toll on farmers in countries from Guatemala to Malawi, alongside eradicating a staple food.

Now researchers say they have made fresh advances in the race to save them from disaster. This month, Yelloway – a research collaboration between Chiquita,
title: Have scientists finally found a way to save the banana from disaster?

author: Maya Yang
description:
New study reveals dramatic population drops in fish, cephalopods and more after the Deepwater Horizon spill

Marine life in the Gulf of Mexico plummeted by about 60% after BP’s 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill and has still not fully recovered, according to a new study.

The April 2010 explosion of an offshore drilling unit 50 miles off the Louisiana coast triggered the largest marine oil spill in history, releasing 134m gallons of oil into the ocean. According to the study published Monday in PNAS, the disaster – which also killed 11 people and injured 17 others – led to the “sudden, severe and persistent declines in the abundance” of marine life for more than a decade.
title: Marine life in Gulf of Mexico has still not fully recovered from 2010 BP oil spill

author: Jon Henley
description:
Polls on 25 October could bring a new political landscape in EU-candidate country where a student-led protest movement has become main opposition

Serbia’s 6.5 million voters go to the polls on 25 October in a watershed parliamentary election characterised by civil unrest, a new political landscape, allegations of irregularities, an uncertain outcome and potentially far-reaching consequences.

Here’s a brief guide to the key issues.

Continue reading...
title: What are the key issues in Serbia’s election – and its potential consequences?

author: Alexis Petridis
description:
(tak:til)
The nine-piece London-based group take a radically fresh approach to traditional music, sounding raging, lo-fi and joyful as they link Britain’s violent past to its present

Those thus far unaware of Shovel Dance Collective’s bracing approach to folk should probably note that their third album is not much interested in breaking newcomers in gently. Everything in Readiness kicks off with a three-song suite that lasts more than 10 minutes and takes you, via a series of dramatic sonic jump-cuts, from a grinding one-note drone to a reel that seems to split the difference between trad folk fiddle-playing and the punishing squall of the Velvet Underground’s Black Angel’s Death Song. It then leaps to Tally Ho! Hark Away!, which sets a hunting song first collected in the late 1940s over a blast of what might best be described as ecstatic noise. It’s genuinely hard to work out what instruments are involved in the clattering arrhythmic chaos behind the voca
title: Shovel Dance Collective: Everything in Readiness review – ecstatic, dissonant folk music fighting for sonic and spiritual freedom

author: Miranda Bryant in Muhos and Otanmäki
description:
Company ordered to stop work at two sites in country, which has found itself at forefront of tech firms’ latest push

Behind a wire fence lies a vast gaping wound of earth. Before Google’s arrival a few months ago, an estimated quarter of a million trees occupied the 330 hectares (815 acres) of forest near the town of Muhos in rural northern Finland. Now they are all gone.

After the tech company illegally stripped the entire area to build a datacentre – taking even the top soil with it – all that remains is a vast expanse of mud indented with the trail marks of machinery, puddles and mounds of earth, roots and branches. Residents say that brown water flowing off the site is going into a stream that feeds the Oulujoki River.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Pure arrogance’: anger in Finland as Google illegally fells 250,000 trees for datacentre

author: Kim Willsher in Paris
description:
Politicians have called for ruthless sentencing, but lawyers blame the politicians for the poverty, and anger, behind their clients’ looting

  • Europe live – latest updates

Awa, 18, stood in the dock in the tribunal de Paris, a small, mute and bewildered figure seeming unable to understand, let alone answer, the simplest of questions.

The court was told she had joined young people who looted an Yves Saint Laurent store on Boulevard Saint Germain in Paris’s Left Bank late on Sunday and stripped it bare within minutes.

Continue reading...
title: Angry lawyers and bewildered defendants: the fallout from fast-tracking French rioting cases

author: Oliver Laughland, Tom Silverstone, Katie Lamborn, Jem Talbot, Ivan Kuraev
description:
A battle for Alabama’s second congressional district is being fought against a backdrop of partisan gerrymandering and America’s ongoing civil rights struggle. Oliver Laughland and Tom Silverstone track down the Maga Republican Rhett Marques who is looking to unseat Democratic incumbent Shomari Figures but won’t answer questions about redistricting. Meanwhile, lower-income residents in rural parts of the district are still fighting for basic sanitation rights after Donald Trump ended federal assistance, which the administration described as 'illegal DEI'.

Continue reading...
title: How Alabama's Republicans are disenfranchising Black voters – video

author: Agence France-Presse in Yangon
description:
Kim Aris says ‘hearing her voice again means more than words can express’ amid loosening of detention restrictions

The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to speak to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years.

“Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express,” Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Aung San Suu Kyi’s son speaks to detained former Myanmar leader for first time in five years

author: Guardian community team
description:
We want to hear from those working or living at sea, including maritime workers, sailors, port staff and family about how the situation is affecting their work

The conflict in the Middle East continues to disrupt shipping across the region, including in the strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s busiest maritime routes.

Iran state TV has reported that seven oil tankers were damaged in the Straight of Hormuz on Wednesday night. There has been an increase in the number of attacks on ships in recent days; some vessels have been hit by drones, others by mines.

Continue reading...
title: Maritime and port workers: how is the Middle East conflict affecting you?

author: Hosted by Carter Sherman and Kai Wright with Sam Levine and George Chidi . Produced by Monica Espitia, engineered by Ivan Kuraev, executive producer Rachel Humphreys
description:
This week, the Department of Justice charged 28 green card holders in California over alleged voter fraud. It’s the latest move by the Trump administration to crack down on noncitizen voters, and part of a wider push to throw the results of the midterms into doubt. In today's episode, Carter Sherman and Kai Wright are joined by George Chidi and Sam Levine, two reporters who have spent years covering Donald Trump’s attacks on voting rights. They analyze the tactics being used to purge voter rolls, and look ahead to how Trump might react if the results on election day don’t go his way.

Continue reading...
title: Is Trump going to steal the midterms? - Stateside with Kai and Carter

author: Alice Hutton
description:
Last year, South Korea took responsibility for enabling the ‘mass export’ of children for sale abroad. Now those uprooted are grappling with false promises of a better life

As international, transracial adoptees in their 30s in the US, Jacquelyn Wells and Lauren White-Gydas have things in common.

They were both born in South Korea to unwed mothers in the 1980s. Both were shipped to the US as newborns to join white families who eagerly welcomed adorable, new daughters. And neither knew many other Asians in the towns where they grew up – Wells in Westford, Massachusetts, and White-Gydas in Salem, Oregon.

Continue reading...
title: Adoptees from Korea say they were isolated and abused in the US. Were they also ‘stolen’ from their birth parents?

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
An estimated 70% of websites use the open-source language. What is the identified vulnerability in it?

Websites across the world have been taken offline in the past day as governments and businesses work to patch newly discovered vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language that underpins much of the internet. The exposed flaw would have allowed hackers to carry out cyber-attacks. What were the vulnerabilities and why did they affect so many sites?

Continue reading...
title: What is PHP, and how bad is the computer language flaw causing website shutdowns globally?

author: Agencies
description:
• Edwards hits nine threes in 45-point explosion

  • Antetokounmpo scores 35 in first game with Heat

  • Minnesota rout Miami 131-106 in season opener

Anthony Edwards scored 45 points as he and the Minnesota Timberwolves spoiled Giannis Antetokounmpo’s debut with the Miami Heat in an emphatic 131-106 season-opening win on Wednesday night.

Edwards became just the third player in NBA history to record multiple 40-point games in season openers, joining Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan.

Continue reading...
title: Anthony Edwards scores 45 as Timberwolves spoil Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Heat debut

author: Juan A Ramírez
description:
Imperial Theatre, New York City
The veteran actor charms with stories about his colorful life and losing his home in the LA fires while taking jabs at Trump

In his review of the 1986 buddy comedy Running Scared, Roger Ebert wrote that Billy Crystal and Gregory Hines, the film’s leads, “don’t need a plot because they have so much good dialogue and such a great screen relationship”. With a bit of paraphrasing, Ebert’s description of that chemistry works just the same when discussing Crystal’s relationship to the New York stage, where the legendary funnyman has made a cozy home for himself this century.

His 2004 one-man show 700 Sundays won a special Tony and was brought back nearly a decade later to be filmed for HBO. Then came Mr Saturday Night in 2022, which Crystal adapted from an earlier movie and which was tepidly, politely received. S
title: 860 review – Billy Crystal’s charisma powers rambling one-man play

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
US envoy Witkoff presented Putin with proposals drafted by Zelenskyy and European leaders in Oslo earlier this week. What we know on day 1,702

The Kremlin has criticised new peace proposals to end the war after US envoy Steve Witkoff met with Russian leader Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday. Commenting on the meeting, which followed talks with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European leaders in Oslo, the Kremlin warned there was little “substance” in the Ukrainian and European proposals. Despite the lukewarm response from Russia, US president Donald Trump claimed it was “the closest we’ve been” to ending the war. A day before travelling to Russia, Witkoff met Zelenskyy and European leaders in Norway in a meeting aimed at smoothing over a bitter rift between the Ukrainian president and Trump.

Commenting on the Witkoff-Putin meeting, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that Russia was “in principle, ready to resume” the
title: Ukraine war briefing: New peace proposals lack ‘substance’, says Kremlin after Witkoff-Putin meeting in Russia

author: Agence France-Presse
description:
Author withdrawn from France’s Prix Goncourt last month has repeatedly denied using artificial intelligence to write novel

The publisher of top-selling Haitian Canadian writer Thélyson Orélien, who was removed from France’s most prestigious literary prize list last month, has confirmed the author used artificial intelligence to help write his novel C’était ça ou mourir (It Was Either That or Die).

Orélien has denied allegations that he used AI on his breakthrough novel and, last week, Canadian publisher Les Éditions du Boréal said it was standing by the 38-year-old writer.

Continue reading...
title: Canadian publisher Boréal ends relationship with novelist Thélyson Orélien over alleged use of AI

author: Presented by Reged Ahmad and Jonathan Yerushalmy ; produced by Lu Hill ; video production by Rachel Herron ; sound and mixing by Lu Hill ; executive producer is Hannah Parkes
description:
In this episode of Guardian Australia’s US politics podcast, co-hosts Jonathan Yerushalmy and Reged Ahmad look at how Katie Zacharia broke the record for shortest tenure as White House press secretary. They then look at the pattern of how women in the Trump administration are treated when they’re perceived to have made mistakes – versus how men seem to survive their missteps.

They also look at how the US might be changing course on Russia’s war on Ukraine. Are relations between the US president, Donald Trump, and the Ukraine president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, at their lowest point ever – and what happens if the US decides to take Russian president Vladimir Putin’s side in this war?

Continue reading...
title: Decoding America: Katie Zacharia and Trump’s women problem – video
